title: A lens and its focal length
hook: Change focal length and predict lens optical power.
misconception: lens optical power doubles when focal length doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply D = 1/f to compare lens optical power when focal length changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a thin lens in air with focal length measured in metres, D = 1/f. When focal length doubles, lens optical power becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model D = 1/f; scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a thin lens in air with focal length measured in metres, with a nonzero initial result. If focal length triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on lens optical power?
recall.why: Apply D = 1/f under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
